newsitem.title: USA: ADM board independence backed by adviser.
newsitem.headline: ADM board independence backed by adviser.

text.p: A proxy advisory firm has come out in support of a shareholder move to require a majority of Archer Daniels Midland Co's board of directors be made up of outsiders.

Maryland-based Institutional Shareholder Services Inc said that although its own guidelines for classifying a director as independent are less stringent than the proposals' sponsors -- two large pension funds -- "we believe that given ADM's governance history, a narrower definition of independence is warranted." But Institutional Shareholders backed management's proposed slate of directors.

California Public employees' Retirement System and Florida Retirement System Trust Fund are making their push for board independence in the wake of a probe by the U.S. Justice Department into alleged price fixing by the company in the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup market.

Decatur, Illinois-based ADM said in proxy materials filed in advance of the October 17 shareholder meeting that it has been informed the company and executive officers Michael Andreas and Terrance Wilson are targets of the lysine investigation and indictments are being considered against them.

Management of the agribusiness giant has proposed cutting the board to 12 from 17 members with three outside and has said it is trying to seek a balance between investors' concerns about board independence and ADM's desire to find the best qualified candidates.

In an analysis dated Thursday, Institutional Shareholder Services also supported shareholder proposals calling for adding women and minorities to ADM's board, calling for cumulative voting for directors and for confidential voting, all of which were opposed by ADM management.
The adviser recommended against establishing personal financial responsibility on the part of directors for gross negligence.
The service also came out against an management proposed stock option plan, but supported a deferred compensation plan proposed by management.
